---
title: "Figure 2.4: US Holdings of Foreign Bonds"
---

![Python: `python/fig-2-4.py`](../images/python/fig-2-4.png)

Three quarterly lines: the share of US holdings of foreign bonds that goes
to each of three emerging-market regions (Latin America 7, emerging Asia and
emerging Europe). The chart shows that LA7 receives a much larger share than
the other two regions.

**New in this chart:** a label for every second quarter only, written
vertically.

## The data

Sheet `data`, 18 rows (2022Q1 onward):

| category | LA7 | EM Asia | EM Europe |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022Q1 | 5.26 | 2.02 | 0.58 |

The `category` column contains text such as `2022Q1`. matplotlib cannot
place text on a numeric axis, so the script plots the quarters at positions
0, 1, 2, ... and then writes the quarter names under those positions. This
is how Excel's category axis works too.

## The script

The script follows the pattern of [Figure 1.1](fig-1-1.qmd), which explains
each step in more detail. Here the focus is on what differs.

### Larger text in the frame

```python
fig, ax = new_chart(
    title="US Holdings of Foreign Bonds",
    subtitle="(Percent share of total world)",
    caption=(...),
    title_size=13.5,
    subtitle_size=11.5,
    left=0.3,
    right=0.2,
    bottom_gap=0.62,
)
```

The published chart has a slightly larger title and subtitle than most REO
charts, so the defaults of `new_chart()` (13 and 11 points) are raised by
half a point. Everything else in the layout adjusts to the new sizes.

`bottom_gap=0.62` is about twice the usual value. The quarter labels are
written vertically and are longer than year labels, so they need more room
between the x-axis and the caption.

### The lines at category positions

```python
x = np.arange(len(data))
for series, colour in series_colours.items():
    ax.plot(x, data[series], color=colour, linewidth=1.8,
            solid_capstyle="round", solid_joinstyle="round", label=series)
```

`np.arange(len(data))` makes the positions 0, 1, ..., 17, one for each row.
See [Categories as positions](../techniques.qmd#sec-categories).

The loop draws one line per region, with the colour from `series_colours`.
`solid_capstyle="round"` rounds the line ends and `solid_joinstyle="round"`
rounds the corners where a line changes direction. Excel draws both round;
matplotlib's defaults are a square end and a sharp corner, which look
spiky on quarterly data with sudden changes. See [Line
styles](../techniques.qmd#sec-line-styles).

### Every second quarter

```python
# Label every second quarter.
ax.set_xticks(x[::2], data["category"].iloc[::2], rotation=90)
ax.set_xlim(0, len(data) - 1)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", direction="in", length=2.3, pad=5, labelsize=9.5)
```

`ax.set_xticks(positions, labels)` sets where the ticks go and what they
say. Both arguments are thinned with `[::2]`, Python's way of taking every
second element, starting with the first. For the positions this gives 0, 2,
4, ...; for the labels `.iloc[::2]` gives the matching rows, 2022Q1,
2022Q3, 2023Q1, .... It is important to thin both in the same way, or the
labels would end up under the wrong quarters.

With 18 quarters, labelling all of them would crowd the axis. This is what
Excel does with *Interval between labels = 2*.

- `rotation=90` writes the labels vertically.
- `ax.set_xlim(0, len(data) - 1)` makes the lines start at the left edge and
  end at the right edge, with no margin, as in the published chart.
- `direction="in"` points the tick marks into the plot instead of out of it.
- `labelsize=9.5` makes the labels half a point larger than the house
  default, to match the published version.

### The y-axis and legend

```python
ax.set_ylim(0, 7)
ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(1))
ax.tick_params(axis="y", direction="in", length=2.3, pad=6, labelsize=9.5)

ax.legend(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.06, 1.0), fontsize=9.5,
          handlelength=3.0, labelspacing=0.15)
```

The y-axis runs from 0 to 7. `MultipleLocator(1)` is matplotlib's
equivalent of Excel's *major unit*: a tick at every multiple of 1. It does
the same job as the helper `set_y_scale(ax, 0, 7, 1)` used in most other
scripts. See [Number formats and tick
spacing](../techniques.qmd#sec-number-formats).

The y-ticks also point inwards, and the labels use 9.5 points. The legend
sits in the top left, where all three lines are low enough to leave room.
`handlelength=3.0` lengthens the line samples and `labelspacing=0.15` keeps
the three entries close together. See [Legends](../techniques.qmd#sec-legends).

## Changing the chart

- **Label every quarter, or every fourth.** Change both `[::2]` to `[::1]`
  or `[::4]`. With `[::4]` only the first quarters (Q1) are labelled.
- **Start with the last quarter.** To make sure the latest quarter has a
  label, thin from the end: `x[::-2][::-1]` and
  `data["category"].iloc[::-2][::-1]`.
- **Horizontal labels.** Remove `rotation=90` and reduce `bottom_gap`, but
  only label every fourth quarter, or the labels will overlap.

## The complete script

The full `python/fig-2-4.py`, as it runs:

```` {.python filename="python/fig-2-4.py"}
"""Figure 2.4: US Holdings of Foreign Bonds."""
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.ticker import MultipleLocator

from chart_style import new_chart, read_chart_data, save_chart

STEM = "fig-2-4"

data = read_chart_data(STEM)

series_colours = {
    "LA7": "#5B267A",
    "EM Asia": "#00A3AD",
    "EM Europe": "#D05A0D",
}

fig, ax = new_chart(
    title="US Holdings of Foreign Bonds",
    subtitle="(Percent share of total world)",
    caption=(
        "Sources: Haver Analytics; and IMF staff calculations.\n"
        "Note: LA7 excludes Paraguay due to data limitations. EM = emerging\n"
        "markets; EM Asia = India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand; EM\n"
        "Europe = Hungary, Poland, Romania, Serbia; LA7 = Latin America 7\n"
        "(Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Paraguay, Peru)."
    ),
    title_size=13.5,
    subtitle_size=11.5,
    left=0.3,
    right=0.2,
    bottom_gap=0.62,
)

x = np.arange(len(data))
for series, colour in series_colours.items():
    ax.plot(x, data[series], color=colour, linewidth=1.8,
            solid_capstyle="round", solid_joinstyle="round", label=series)

# Label every second quarter.
ax.set_xticks(x[::2], data["category"].iloc[::2], rotation=90)
ax.set_xlim(0, len(data) - 1)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", direction="in", length=2.3, pad=5, labelsize=9.5)

ax.set_ylim(0, 7)
ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(1))
ax.tick_params(axis="y", direction="in", length=2.3, pad=6, labelsize=9.5)

ax.legend(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.06, 1.0), fontsize=9.5,
          handlelength=3.0, labelspacing=0.15)

save_chart(fig, STEM)
````
